articles.title: CLAUDE WAS TRAINED ON PROTEIN SEQUENCES AT SCALE
articles.summary: Tests show that the latest Claude models were trained on protein sequences at scale. The models can predict the next amino acid if given the start of little-studied bacterial proteins. No other model tested can do this, and the models fail to predict the sequence if the protein is shuffled. Fable 5.2 beats every open protein language model tested.

articles.title: WORLD 2030
articles.summary: Predicting how AI will affect the economy requires looking at all of the different components of that economy and figuring out how they might affect each other. World 2030 is a study that sets up nine groups (AI labs, big employers, banks and insurers, utilities, startups, universities, workers, governments, and the Fed) and runs the US economy forward in six-month turns to 2030. It aimed to identify both the invariants and the boundaries of what can change as these powerful forces interact with each other. The study predicts that AI will break per-seat software pricing and cut US junior desk hiring.

articles.title: MEASURING ALIGNMENT EVAL TELLS
articles.summary: Investigator agents can increasingly distinguish alignment evals from capabilities evals, identifying them as artificial or "honeypot" environments designed to test bad behavior. Opus 5.5 and Astra agents differentiate these by noticing unrealistic scenarios and specific task-level cues. The study's findings suggest that while current models can identify common alignment evaluations, making them less detectable can refine their efficacy.

D1.2: STATE-OF-THE-ART OMNIMODAL DECISION MODELS
articles.summary: d1.2 and d1.2-ultra are decision models that support audio input. They can also read a value from the input, find every passage of a kind in a text, locate things in a picture, estimate a number, and pick every option that applies. d1.2-ultra ranks first among decision models on the Artificial Analysis Decision Index v2.1. Both models are available on the Liquid API at $0.02 per million input tokens for d1.2 and $0.042 per million input tokens for d1.2-ultra.

articles.title: HUGGING FACE AND OPENROUTER JOIN FORCES
articles.summary: Hugging Face now routes language-model requests from its Inference Providers service through OpenRouter, which picks the best provider for each call. A single Hugging Face access token works for any open-weight model a provider serves.

articles.title: UNLOCKING STABLE ON-POLICY RL ON TPU WITH BITWISE-ZERO TRAIN–INFERENCE MISMATCH
articles.summary: Google's ZERO-TIM implementation, verified across 64 TPU v5p chips, achieves bitwise-identical logprobs for sampler and trainer, ensuring true on-policy stability in RL training by eliminating numerical discrepancies. This solution addresses floating-point addition errors in separate serving and training paths, using consistent arithmetic operations and standardized reduction orders across TPU meshes.

articles.title: OPENAI'S FIRST PHASE OF EMBEDDED ASSESSMENTS
articles.summary: Embedded assessments give independent experts deep access to a lab's internal models and systems so they can assess model alignment and the effectiveness of safeguards over an extended period. The access gives assessors the evidence and context to pursue independent evaluations and uncover unanticipated failures. Public reporting from independent assessments can give the public a clearer view of how labs are evaluating and managing risks. OpenAI has signed agreements with four independent assessors for its first phase of embedded assessments.

articles.title: THE FRONTIER IS STILL OPEN
articles.summary: Perplexity Frontier Research is a new initiative at Perplexity that aims to build new algorithms, models, and evaluations in the open, with the mission of building an automated scientist.
